tutorials.description: Download the latest FreeEQ8 release (VST3 / AU / Standalone for macOS, Windows, Linux), place the plugin in your DAW's scan path — macOS ~/Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/VST3, Windows C:\Program Files\Common Files\VST3, Linux ~/.vst3 — then rescan. Tested in Ableton Live 10+, REAPER, Logic Pro, FL Studio and Bitwig. Also installable via StudioRack: studiorack plugin install garebear99/freeeq8.
tutorials.name: Install FreeEQ8 in Your DAW

tutorials.description: A guided tour of this dashboard: the Plugins tab lists all 20 free plugins with live GitHub release checks, Packs & Samples holds the 11 free sample packs, Tools has the browser-playable Instrudio instruments, and the Lists tab starts at awesome-audio-plugins-dev — the Start Here list for the whole ecosystem. Every product has a free version; payments and upgrades live inside each product, never on the HUB.
tutorials.name: Find Your First Free Plugin, Pack or Tool on the HUB

tutorials.description: Clone with submodules (git clone --recursive https://github.com/GareBear99/FreeEQ8.git — JUCE 7.0.12 is a submodule), then build with the shipped scripts: ./build_macos.sh, ./build_linux.sh, or .\build_windows.ps1. The built VST3 lands in build/FreeEQ8_artefacts/Release/VST3/. FreeEQ8 is GPL-3.0, so your changes stay open when you share them.
tutorials.name: Build FreeEQ8 from Source with JUCE + CMake

tutorials.description: FreeVox8 is a JUCE spectral vocoder with a 128-band log-spaced vocoder core, Spectral Ghost 1024 backend, MIDI-controlled internal carrier, sidechain modulator bus, and Vocoder / Mask / Ghost / Morph modes. JUCE is intentionally not vendored: add it with git submodule add https://github.com/juce-framework/JUCE.git JUCE (or pass -DJUCE_DIR), then cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release && cmake --build build --config Release. Validate the package with python3 scripts/validate_repo.py.
tutorials.name: Build FreeVox8 from Source: a JUCE Spectral Vocoder

tutorials.description: FreeEQ8's documented surgical recipe: a Bell filter with narrow Q (6–12) and −6 to −12 dB of gain on the offending frequency. Worked examples from the FreeEQ8 docs — kick drum cardboard at 200 Hz (Bell, Q=3, −3 dB), acoustic-guitar boominess at 200 Hz (Bell, Q=1.5, −2 dB), vocal muddiness at 250 Hz (Bell, Q=2, −3 dB). Use the real-time spectrum analyzer to find the frequency before you cut it.
tutorials.name: Surgical EQ with FreeEQ8: Remove Problem Frequencies

tutorials.description: FreeEQ8's documented musical-EQ recipe: wide Bell or Shelf filters (Q 0.5–2) with gentle ±3 to ±6 dB moves, plus a HighPass at 20–120 Hz (Q 0.7) to clear rumble. Worked examples — kick sub thump at 60 Hz (+4 dB), acoustic-guitar presence at 3 kHz (+3 dB) with air from a HighShelf at 8 kHz (+2 dB), vocal body at 1 kHz (+2 dB) and clarity at 5 kHz (+3 dB). Small, wide moves beat big, narrow ones for tone.
tutorials.name: Musical EQ: Broad Tonal Shaping with FreeEQ8

tutorials.description: All 11 HUB sample packs are free and royalty-free (see each repo). The Free 808 Producer Kit has 94 hand-crafted 808s tuned to every chromatic key; the Free Riser Producer Kit has 115+ risers and 63 downlifters; the Free Dark Piano Sound Kit covers 88 piano notes plus dark and cinematic loops and MIDI; the Phonk Producer Toolkit ships 808s, cowbells, drums, MIDI and templates. Drag the WAVs into any DAW sampler or timeline — no installer, no account.
tutorials.name: Using the Free Sample Packs in Your DAW

tutorials.description: How the pieces connect: a free plugin such as FreeEQ8 brings producers to the HUB; the HUB routes them into the awesome-audio-plugins-dev Start Here list, the free sample packs and browser tools (Instrudio, Voxel Audio, BannerBass); finished music goes through the Release Vault for distribution proof on SoundCloud, YouTube and Spotify. The HUB itself never takes payment — upgrades live inside each product, and checkout for itch assets happens on itch.io.
tutorials.name: The TizWildin Ecosystem, End to End
